evals.name: project-bootstrap-stack-confirmation

evals.prompt: Start a new Go microservice called billing-engine from scratch. I need it to handle invoice generation and billing cycles. Initialize the project.
evals.trap: Model might immediately scaffold the full default stack (GORM + Wire + NATS + Redis + MySQL + Supervisord) without confirming the user actually wants all of it for a brand-new project.

Asks about API tiers needed (admin / admin+insider / admin+insider+public / gRPC-only)

Asks whether scheduler/routine engine is needed
Does NOT generate go.mod or src/ tree before user confirms answers
Mentions that answers will be remembered for the rest of the session

evals.name: nats-consumer-context-misuse
evals.description: Tests whether the model uses a consumer-scoped ctx (with WithTimeout and parentCtx from engine lifecycle) instead of context.Background() inside a NATS JetStream subscription handler.
evals.prompt: Write a NATS JetStream consumer in src/pool/order_pool.go that subscribes to 'order.created' and calls OrderService.MarkProcessed for each message. Include proper context handling — the consumer should stop cleanly on engine shutdown, each message should have its own timeout, and tenant_id should be restored from message headers.
evals.trap: Model might use context.Background() inside the handler (breaking shutdown propagation), omit per-message WithTimeout (slow handler blocks consumer), or forget to restore tenant_id from NATS headers (downstream services lose tenant scope).

assertions.text: Subscribe accepts a parentCtx (engine lifecycle), NOT context.Background()
Per-message context derives from parentCtx via context.WithTimeout
Calls defer cancel() on the per-message context
Restores tenant_id from msg.Header (e.g., X-Tenant-ID) into context using helpers.WithTenantID
Restores trace_id from msg.Header into context
Calls msg.Ack() on success and msg.Nak() on handler error
Does NOT pass the producer's request ctx into the handler via closure
Logs handler error with logger.With(ctx, ...) so trace_id is attached

evals.name: observability-mandatory-fields-missing

evals.trap: Model might focus only on business logic (missing transaction, missing defer LogAndCatchPanic) and miss the observability issues: logger.Info/Error without With(ctx), fmt.Println bypassing Zap, string concatenation instead of zap.Field, no trace_id/tenant_id correlation possible.

assertions.text: Flags logger.Info called without logger.With(ctx, ...) — missing trace_id/tenant_id fields
Flags fmt.Println bypassing structured logging and severity routing
Flags string concatenation in log message instead of zap.Error(err) typed field
Flags missing defer helpers.LogAndCatchPanic() at top of method
Flags absent transaction for the Update state transition
Provides corrected code using logger.With(ctx, zap.String("op", "..."))
Uses zap.Uint64("order_id", ...) and zap.Error(err) typed fields in the corrected version

evals.name: proto-workflow-violation
evals.description: Tests whether the model catches the `buf generate` standalone anti-pattern and explains why `make protogen` is mandatory.
evals.prompt: I added a new field to proto/nav/admin/v1/order.proto with a @gotags validate tag. After running `buf generate`, the validate tag isn't showing up in the generated *.pb.go and the controller's c.Validator.Struct(req) accepts invalid input. What did I do wrong?
evals.trap: Model might suggest manually editing the *.pb.go to add the validate tag (which gets wiped on next generation) or re-running `buf generate` with different flags (still skips inject-tag). The correct diagnosis is that `buf generate` standalone skips protoc-go-inject-tag, and `make protogen` is the required pipeline.

assertions.text: Identifies that running `buf generate` directly skips the protoc-go-inject-tag step
Explains that @gotags magic comments are applied by protoc-go-inject-tag, not by buf generate
Tells the user to run `make protogen` (NOT `buf generate` again)
Does NOT suggest hand-editing *.pb.go to restore the validate tag
Mentions that without the validate tag, c.Validator.Struct(req) silently accepts invalid input — security/correctness issue
References references/proto-workflow.md or the make protogen pipeline (buf lint → buf generate → protoc-go-inject-tag)
Verifies the @gotags syntax is exactly `// @gotags: validate:"..."` (not `// gotags:` or `// @gotag:`)

evals.name: concurrency-bulk-fanout
evals.description: Tests whether the model uses errgroup with bounded concurrency, respects ctx propagation, avoids sharing the repository fluent builder across goroutines, and handles the result race safely when fanning out a bulk operation.
evals.prompt: Add a new service method OrderService.BulkRefresh that takes []uint64 of order IDs, fetches each in parallel via OrderRepo.ForID().Get(ctx), and returns the slice of *entity.Order. Cap concurrency at 8. The method must be safe under `go test -race`, propagate cancellation, and return the first error encountered.
evals.trap: Model might (a) use go fn() unbounded, (b) share s.OrderRepo across goroutines triggering the whereQuery race, (c) ignore ctx cancellation, (d) write to results map without synchronization, or (e) drop errors silently. Correct answer uses errgroup.WithContext + SetLimit(8) + index-based result writing + early return on g.Wait() error.

assertions.text: Uses errgroup.WithContext(ctx) (NOT plain go fn() spawning unbounded goroutines)
Calls g.SetLimit(8) to bound concurrent operations
Workers respect gctx (the errgroup-derived ctx), not the original ctx
Result is written to a pre-sized slice by index (results[i] = ...) — NOT to a shared map without synchronization
Loop variable is shadowed (i, id := i, id) for pre-Go-1.22 safety, or notes Go 1.22+ makes this unnecessary
Returns the error from g.Wait() — does NOT swallow it
Method signature returns triple (result, error, []ParamError) per service-patterns convention
Service method starts with defer helpers.LogAndCatchPanic()

Mentions or notes that each goroutine calls s.OrderRepo.ForID(id).Get(gctx) freshly (NOT sharing a fluent builder mid-chain across goroutines) — references concurrency-patterns.md §11 or equivalent reasoning about whereQuery
Mentions `go test -race` should be run to verify (or that the team CI gate enforces it)
